currentContext.business: Airan Limited is, in its secretarial auditor's words, mainly engaged in the business of information technology and IT-enabled services including banking transaction services and document management services for telecommunication companies, internet service providers and payment banks. The MD&A describes the business as organised around three interconnected capabilities - operations, technology and consulting - with accumulated experience across banking operations, transaction processing, trade-related services, workforce solutions and customer engagement, delivered both domestically and internationally. The Company states it is operational in a single segment; internationally it runs operations in Thailand integrated with the local financial infrastructure ecosystem and develops UK and Australian business through the Airan Global subsidiary, with further subsidiaries in Singapore, Australia, the UK, plus Cqub Infosystems and Quadpro ITeS.

currentContext.expansion: Airan's expansion in FY 2025-26 is described entirely as footprint, capability and delivery-scope build-out rather than as physical capacity or a capex programme; the routed text contains no plant, site or capacity project and no rupee capex quantum. Geographically, the Company says it continued to deepen its presence in the Asia-Pacific region, with operations in Thailand expanding further and achieving greater integration with the local financial infrastructure ecosystem, while the Group continued to develop its international business through Airan Global with increasing engagement across the United Kingdom and Australia. The Chairman & Managing Director's letter frames the same move as entering new markets and becoming involved in more critical parts of clients' operations, with Airan Global 'opening up a much larger opportunity for us across the UK and Australia'. Commercially, the Company says it expanded the scope of several existing engagements, moving beyond individual processes towards broader and more integrated client relationships, and lists an expanded presence in voice and contact-centre services among the opportunities it is pursuing. Capability build-out is technology- and people-led: during the year the Company continued to strengthen internal software platforms and explore the practical integration of artificial intelligence into operational workflows, with automation engines, intelligent workflow tools and AI-assisted applications described as creating opportunities to redesign traditionally manpower-intensive processes; it states it increased its workforce capabilities during the year and had a total workforce of 1512 employees as of March 31, 2026. Forward-looking items are stated as intentions, not completed projects: Airan 'intends' to combine its technology capabilities with its operational experience to develop customised solutions particularly within banking, financial services and knowledge-process environments, and for FY 2026-27 'intends to deepen existing relationships, expand selectively across international markets and progressively increase the contribution of consulting-led, technology-enabled and managed solutions to its overall business'. No commissioning dates, site names, project costs or timelines are disclosed in the routed text.
